# Research report 1 of 2

Note: the system reports a later date than the exercise date. I excluded everything published after 2026-09-22, including later figures that turned up in search results.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the AAA "Current Avg." for regular gasoline at gasprices.aaa.com on 2026-10-01. I could not open the page directly because the proxy refused the connection, so the AAA figures below come from search snippets and news coverage.
- 2026-09-22: AAA's national average for regular was **$4.47/gal**. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/gas-prices-09-22-26-142109950.html), headline: "National average remains well over $4.40 per gallon"
- 2026-09-17: AAA's weekly release put the average at **$4.43**, up 16 cents in a week and more than $1 above a year earlier. AAA said the rise came from crude averaging about $100/bbl. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. On 2026-09-22 the average was about **7 cents above** the $4.400 threshold. It would need to fall more than about 7 cents in roughly 9 days to resolve NO.
- 2026-09-21: Other trackers agree on the level. GasBuddy had $4.44, up 18.5 cents in a week. EIA's weekly regular price was $4.478. [GasBuddy/Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/gas-prices-09-22-26-142109950.html), [FRED GASREGW](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GASREGW)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-22: AAA was at $4.47. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan said diesel had not yet peaked. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/gas-prices-09-22-26-142109950.html)
- 2026-09-21: Brent was about **$101.61/bbl** at 9:35 a.m. ET, down about $2.72 from the previous business day. That points to some easing in crude. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/article/price-of-oil-09-21-2026/)
- 2026-09-16: De Haan reported GasBuddy's live gasoline average at $4.355 and diesel at $6.301, and expected both to "jump noticeably over the next 48 hours." [X/@GasBuddyGuy](https://x.com/GasBuddyGuy/status/2100051482049405197)
- 2026-09-13: AAA had regular at about $4.22 and diesel at about $5.94. Coverage tied the high prices to the US-Iran conflict. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/us-gas-prices-hit-priciest-152600337.html)
- 2026-09-08: Oil rose to about $99 on a report that Iran had attacked US Navy ships, with the Strait of Hormuz in focus. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/08/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-iran-war.html)
- Background: this is a 2026 fuel crisis linked to the Iran war, with attacks on tankers and Middle East oil infrastructure. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_fuel_crisis)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- AAA weekly path: 09-03 $4.14, 09-10 $4.27 (+13c), 09-17 $4.43 (+16c), 09-22 $4.47. Prices have risen steadily all month, but the pace slowed to about 4 cents over the last 5 days. [AAA search snippets](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- The 2026 high so far is **$4.564**, set on 2026-05-21. In late July the average was $4.12. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/prediction-markets/how-high-will-gas-prices-get-kalshi-odds)
- Typical variation: in this volatile period, weekly moves of 10 to 18 cents have been common in both directions. In calm years, 9-day moves are usually under 5 cents. Retail prices follow wholesale and crude with a lag of roughly 1 to 2 weeks, and they usually fall more slowly than they rise.
- Seasonal factor: the switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline after September 15 normally pushes prices down from late September into October.
- The 2026-09-21 dip in Brent, if it lasts, would start pulling retail prices down. Whether they fall 7+ cents in 9 days is the key uncertainty.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold price for this specific October 1 contract.
- 2026-09-14: On Kalshi's annual-maximum ladder (highest AAA daily average in 2026), "above $4.60" traded at 74c bid / 76c ask, up from 61c/65c on 09-10. So the market expected prices to go higher in mid-September. [Odds Shopper](https://www.oddsshopper.com/articles/prediction-markets/gas-prices-2026-model-verdict?mp=mid-a3)
- Kalshi lists weekly AAA contracts (KXAAAGASW series), but I found no current price for the week ending around October 1. [Laika Labs](https://laikalabs.ai/app/prediction-markets/kalshi/kxaaagasw-26aug10-4.080)
- Manifold has a similar series ("US average gas price is $4.100 or more"), but I found no probability for this threshold. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Jack1/us-average-gas-price-is-4100-or-mor)
- GasBuddy's January 2026 outlook expected the yearly average under $3. The war has made that forecast obsolete. [GasBuddy](https://www.gasbuddy.com/go/2026-fuel-price-outlook)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (by about 2026-10-01 08:15 UTC)
- Daily AAA updates. Watch whether the average peaks soon after 09-22 or keeps rising toward the May high of $4.564.
- Iran conflict: new attacks on tankers or Gulf infrastructure, or any ceasefire or agreement, could move crude by $5 to $10 or more.
- Restoration of Gulf export routes such as pipeline repairs, plus any SPR release or state fuel-tax suspensions. Newsweek reported earlier that tax suspensions were lowering prices in some states.
- EIA weekly gasoline price and inventory reports (around 09-28/09-30), GasBuddy's weekly report (09-28), and AAA's Thursday release (09-24).
- Refinery outages and late-season hurricanes affecting the Gulf Coast.

**Bottom line:** As of 2026-09-22 AAA was at $4.47, about 7 cents above the threshold. Crude eased slightly on 09-21, but retail prices were still rising slowly. No prediction market price for this exact question was found.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I'm writing up the findings now, using only information dated on or before 2026-09-22. The AAA site and several article pages refused the connection, so the AAA figures below come from search snippets and press coverage.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the AAA "current avg" for regular gas on gasprices.aaa.com on 2026-10-01. I couldn't load the page directly because the proxy refused it. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/)
- 2026-09-22: Coverage citing AAA put the national average for regular at **$4.47**. The headline says the average "remains well over $4.40." [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/gas-prices-09-22-26-142109535.html)
- 2026-09-17: AAA's weekly report put the average at $4.43, up 16 cents from a week earlier. A snippet of AAA's daily data gives one exact figure of $4.4386. [AAA newsroom](https://newsroom.aaa.com/2026/09/national-average-climbs-nearly-5-cents-since-last-week/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. On 2026-09-22 the average was about $4.47, roughly 7 cents above the $4.40 threshold, with 9 days to go. A drop of more than about 7 cents by October 1 would resolve it No; holding flat or rising would resolve it Yes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-22: Brent was about $99.9 a barrel and WTI about $95.3. Iran signaled it could reopen transit through the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports. No deal had been announced. [Mezha](https://mezha.net/eng/?p=3726310)
- About 2026-09-20: ABC reported the average was nearing $4.48 and diesel hit a record $6.49. It also said 2026 set a record for the most days above $4 in a calendar year. [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Business/gas-prices-set-record-highest-number-days-4/story?id=137253203)
- 2026-09-17: AAA's report "Pump Prices Keep Climbing as Crude Oil Remains High" said crude was averaging about $100 a barrel and prices were more than $1 above a year earlier. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- 2026-09-10: AAA put the average at $4.27, up 13 cents in a week as crude climbed. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- 2026-09-03: AAA put the average at $4.14, up 4 cents in a week. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- Industry groups say both global supply shocks (Hormuz, Venezuela) and limited US refinery capacity are pushing pump prices up. [CNY Central](https://cnycentral.com/news/nation-world/gallery/oil-group-says-global-supply-shocks-us-refinery-limits-are-both-driving-pump-pain-gulf-coast-venezuela-strait-hormuz?photo=1)

## 4. Base rates
- **Trend:** about $4.10 in late August, $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and about $4.47 on Sept 22. That is roughly a 37-cent rise in a month, but the rise slowed to about +4 cents between Sept 17 and Sept 22.
- **2026 high so far:** $4.564 on May 21. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/prediction-markets/how-high-will-gas-prices-get-kalshi-odds)
- **Typical size of moves:** In calm periods the AAA average usually moves less than 5 cents over 9 days. In shock periods like 2022 and September 2026 it can move 10 to 20 cents a week. Retail prices typically react to a change in crude within about 1 to 2 weeks and fall more slowly than they rise ("rockets and feathers"). That is general knowledge, not something I found in a source.
- **Seasonal pattern:** After the switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline (allowed from Sept 15), prices usually drift lower from late September into October, unless crude or refinery shocks override it.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi runs weekly and monthly AAA gas-price markets (series KXAAAGASW and KXAAAGASM). I couldn't find prices for October 1 thresholds dated on or before the cutoff. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/category/economics/oil-and-energy)
- Manifold has related markets, for example "US average gas price is $4.100 or more." I didn't retrieve their probabilities. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Jack1/us-average-gas-price-is-4100-or-mor)
- Spring 2026: Treasury Secretary Bessent was optimistic gas could return to about $3 between June 20 and September 20. That clearly did not happen. [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/nation-world/scott-bessent-says-gas-could-be-3-between-june-and-september-treasury-donald-trump-oil-strait-of-hormuz-iran)

## 6. Upcoming events before October 1
- **Iran and Hormuz:** a possible reopening within about a week, or a US-Iran deal, could push crude down sharply. Any new escalation, such as more strikes, would push prices up. Because pump prices lag crude, only a crude move in the next few days would show up fully by October 1.
- **EIA weekly petroleum status reports:** about Sept 23 and Sept 30, covering gasoline inventories and refinery utilization.
- **AAA weekly update:** about Sept 24.
- **Hurricane season:** still active, so a storm hitting Gulf Coast refineries remains a risk.
- **Winter-blend transition:** continuing seasonal downward pressure.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- No: A US-Iran arrangement on Hormuz is announced within the next few days and Brent falls $10 or more. Wholesale gasoline then drops 20 to 30 cents and retail falls 1 to 2 cents a day from a roughly $4.48 peak, reaching about $4.38 by October 1.
- Yes: Crude stays in the $95 to $105 range with no deal. Retail plateaus around $4.45 to $4.50 and drifts down only a few cents, ending at about $4.43 to $4.48.

**(f) From base rate to final:** I start at about 80%. Still-rising retail prices and the slow pass-through of crude declines push slightly up. The live Hormuz reopening signal, the crude dip and the seasonal headwind push slightly down, and the 7-cent cushion is thin for a period this volatile. A No outcome most likely needs a sharp crude drop in the next 3 to 5 days, which I put at roughly 15 to 20%, plus a small chance of a faster-than-expected drift lower. These roughly cancel, so I stay near the base rate.

Probability: 79%
